Implicit surfaces fitted to point clouds

Source: R/layers-reconstruct.R
stat_implicit_fit_3d.Rd

Fits a function s(x) whose zero set passes through the points and draws that level surface. Surface triangles face increasing s, outwards.

Usage

stat_implicit_fit_3d(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  geom = GeomStatsSurface3D,
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  method = "rbf",
  n = 32L,
  k = 10L,
  smooth = 0,
  depth = 8L,
  screening = 4,
  samples_per_node = 1.5,
  extractor = NULL,
  refine = 2L,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE
)

Arguments

mapping, data, position, ..., na.rm, show.legend, inherit.aes

Standard layer arguments.

geom

Geom prototype for keyed triangle corners.

method

Fitting method, "rbf" or "poisson".

n

Grid resolution for the "rbf" extraction, scalar or three integers.

k

Number of neighbours for normal estimation and, for "poisson", for the area per point.

smooth

Value added to the diagonal of the "rbf" interpolation matrix; positive values trade interpolation for smoothness.

depth

Maximum octree depth of the "poisson" fit, from 1 to 10; the finest cells are at least 1.1 / 2^depth of the largest extent of the points.

screening

Weight of the point values against the normal field in the "poisson" fit (PoissonRecon's point weight); 0 gives unscreened Poisson reconstruction.

samples_per_node

Number of points an octree cell should meet at the depth where a point is splatted in the "poisson" fit.

extractor

Isosurface extraction method, as method in stat_isosurface_3d(); NULL uses "cubes" for "rbf" and "nets" for "poisson", which takes "nets" or "dual".

refine

Number of regula falsi steps per edge vertex.

Details

method = "rbf" is the polyharmonic radial basis function fit of Carr et al. (2001): s(x) = sum_i w_i |x - c_i| + p(x) with a linear polynomial p, the biharmonic spline in three dimensions, interpolating s = 0 at every point and s = +e and -e at two off-surface points moved by e along the point's normal outwards and inwards. e starts at 1 % of the bounding box diagonal and is halved for a point until that point is the data point nearest to both of its off-surface points. The (3n + 4)-square system is solved densely, so at most 2000 points are taken. s is sampled on an n-point grid over the bounding box of the points, enlarged on each side by 10 % of its extent plus 5 % of its diagonal, and its zero set is extracted as in stat_isofunction_3d with extractor as the extraction method, refine regula falsi steps per edge vertex and vertex normals from s.

method = "poisson" is screened Poisson surface reconstruction (Kazhdan and Hoppe 2013), for large point sets. Each point's surface area is estimated from the disc reaching its k-th nearest neighbour, and its normal is splatted, as a kernel of that area, at the octree depth where a cell meets about samples_per_node points (interpolated between the two nearest depths). The octree, of maximum depth depth, spans a cube 1.1 times the largest extent of the points, enlarged where needed so that it reaches two splat cells beyond every point. The octree is complete to depth 5 and conforming, so every node sees the functions of the coarser nodes around it. The indicator function chi is a combination of quadratic B-splines, one per octree node at every depth, reflected at the cube faces (Neumann boundary), and minimises the squared distance of its gradient to the splatted normal field plus screening times the mean squared value of chi at the points, scaled by the surface area; the screening of depth d is weighted by 2^d. The system is solved by one cascadic pass from the root down, each depth by conjugate gradients with the coarser solution fixed (Kazhdan and Hoppe 2013, algorithm 2). The surface is the level of chi at its mean over the points, extracted on the leaves of the octree by surface nets (extractor = "nets", the default for this method, which placed vertices closer to smooth test surfaces) or dual contouring ("dual"), with refine regula falsi steps per crossing and normals from the gradient of chi. screening = 0 gives the unscreened reconstruction of Kazhdan, Bolitho and Hoppe (2006). The parameters follow PoissonRecon: depth, screening (--pointWeight) and samples_per_node (--samplesPerNode); larger samples_per_node smooths noisy points.

Normals come from the nx, ny and nz aesthetics when all three are mapped. Otherwise each point's normal is the least principal axis of its k nearest neighbours, and normals are oriented consistently by propagation along a minimum spanning tree of the neighbour graph weighted by 1 - |n_i . n_j|, starting at the highest point with an upward normal (Hoppe et al. 1992); a closed surface then gets outward normals.

References

Carr, Beatson, Cherrie, Mitchell, Fright, McCallum and Evans (2001). Reconstruction and representation of 3D objects with radial basis functions. SIGGRAPH 2001, 67-76. doi:10.1145/383259.383266

Hoppe, DeRose, Duchamp, McDonald and Stuetzle (1992). Surface reconstruction from unorganized points. SIGGRAPH 1992, 71-78. doi:10.1145/133994.134011

Kazhdan, Bolitho and Hoppe (2006). Poisson surface reconstruction. Symposium on Geometry Processing 2006, 61-70.

Kazhdan and Hoppe (2013). Screened Poisson surface reconstruction. ACM Transactions on Graphics 32, 29. doi:10.1145/2487228.2487237

Examples

set.seed(2)
p <- matrix(rnorm(450), ncol = 3)
p <- p / sqrt(rowSums(p^2))
d <- data.frame(x = p[, 1], y = p[, 2], z = 0.6 * p[, 3])
ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z)) +
  stat_implicit_fit_3d(n = 20, fill = "steelblue") + coord_3d()

# Screened Poisson reconstruction of a noisy torus from 5000 points
u <- runif(5000, 0, 2 * pi); v <- runif(5000, 0, 2 * pi)
torus <- data.frame(x = (1 + 0.4 * cos(v)) * cos(u), y = (1 + 0.4 * cos(v)) * sin(u),
                    z = 0.4 * sin(v) + rnorm(5000, sd = 0.005))
ggplot2::ggplot(torus, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z)) +
  stat_implicit_fit_3d(method = "poisson", depth = 6, fill = "steelblue") + coord_3d()
